description: Sistema adaptativo de vigilancia fisiológica para la exploración humana del espacio profundo. Más allá de la Tierra, cada señal del cuerpo cuenta una historia y cada decisión puede marcar la diferencia. Heliosync integra datos fisiológicos para reconocer cambios, comprender riesgos y ofrecer alertas claras y oportunas, ayudando a los astronautas a cuidar su salud mientras exploran lo desconocido.
summary:
PROJECT SUMMARY

Long-duration space missions pose health challenges. Radiation, microgravity, isolation, confinement, circadian disruption, and restricted habitats may affect physiological systems. Risks include cardiovascular changes, immune dysregulation, bone and muscle loss, sleep disorders, psychological stress, and neurological and cognitive changes.

HELIOSYNC proposes a platform to collect, analyze, and visualize astronaut health indicators against individual baselines. Six modules address: (1) cardiovascular health; (2) mental health and sleep; (3) immune surveillance; (4) bone, musculoskeletal, and metabolic health; (5) neurological and cognitive function; and (6) rehabilitation and functional performance.

An aerospace medicine and environmental layer will contextualize data by radiation, altered gravity, activity, rest, and habitat conditions. Trend analysis, baseline comparison, data-quality assessment, and explainable AI will flag changes for review.

HELIOSYNC will not replace medical personnel or make autonomous diagnoses. It will provide traceable information to support astronaut self-monitoring and communication with medical professionals.

Research hypothesis: Integrating personalized baselines, temporal persistence, measurement quality, and cross-indicator coherence may improve interpretation of physiological changes beyond general thresholds alone.
details:
5. PROJECT DETAILS

5.1. Technological Architecture

HELIOSYNC will be organized into interconnected functional modules designed to support comprehensive physiological monitoring and multisystem data analysis.

Module 1. Data Acquisition

This module will receive information from compatible sensors, functional assessments, astronaut records, biomedical instruments, and laboratory results.

Module 2. Data Validation and Quality Control

It will detect missing data, incorrectly formatted values, duplicate records, outdated measurements, and potential inconsistencies.

Module 3. Individual Physiological Profile

It will establish a personalized baseline using valid measurements collected in their appropriate context. Baseline updates will be subject to controls to prevent sustained physiological changes from being automatically incorporated as the individual's new normal state.

Module 4. Multisystem Analysis Engine

It will examine trends, temporal persistence, deviations from individual baselines, and relationships between indicators supported by scientific evidence.

Module 5. Alert Engine

It will classify notifications according to their informational relevance, evidence quality, and need for further review. It will not establish medical diagnoses.

Module 6. Visualization Dashboard

It will display charts, indicators, historical records, alerts, explanations, and synchronization status.

Module 7. Security and Data Storage

It will manage access permissions, encryption, audit logs, local storage, and secure synchronization.

5.2. Experimental Physiological Coherence and Evidence Index (ICEF)

HELIOSYNC proposes the development of an experimental indicator called the Physiological Coherence and Evidence Index (ICEF), designed to organize the available evidence concerning physiological changes.

The index will consider five dimensions:

  1. Magnitude of deviation from the individual's baseline.
  2. Temporal persistence of the observed change.
  3. Quality and reliability of measurements.
  4. Data sufficiency and availability.
  5. Coherence among related indicators, when supported by physiological justification.

ICEF will not be presented as a validated biomarker, recognized clinical scale, or diagnostic instrument. It will constitute a methodological proposal requiring definition, testing, and comparison with simpler approaches.

The research will assess whether this approach offers advantages over fixed thresholds and basic individual-baseline comparisons.

5.3. Proposed Technologies

The proposed technological infrastructure includes:

  • Python: data processing and analysis.
  • JavaScript and React: user interface development.
  • HTML and CSS: responsive web visualization.
  • SQLite: initial local data storage.
  • Pandas and NumPy: data manipulation and processing.
  • SciPy and scikit-learn: statistical analysis and preliminary models.
  • Plotly or equivalent libraries: data visualization and graphical representation.
  • Pytest: software testing.
  • Git and GitHub: version control and collaborative development.

Final technology selection will depend on the team's capabilities and the available development time.

5.4. Security, Privacy, and Ethics

Health information is particularly sensitive. Accordingly, the system's design will incorporate the following safeguards:

  • Encryption of stored and transmitted data.
  • Role-based access control according to authorized responsibilities.
  • Pseudonymization of identifiers.
  • Logging of data access and modifications.
  • Minimization of personal information.
  • Consent management whenever applicable.
  • Specific protection of psychological and mental health information.
  • Separation of simulated data from real human data.
  • Backup and data recovery procedures.

Testing involving real human information will require the corresponding ethical and legal authorizations.

5.5. Prototype Evaluation

The system will be evaluated through simulated scenarios and, whenever feasible, suitable public datasets.

The evaluation will examine:

  • Data-processing accuracy.
  • Sensitivity and specificity in defined testing scenarios.
  • False alerts per observation period.
  • Detection time for simulated changes.
  • Performance when data are missing.
  • Consistency of generated alerts.
  • Offline operational capability.
  • Data recovery and synchronization.
  • Clarity and comprehensibility of explanations.
  • User-interface usability.

No claims of clinical efficacy or validation in astronauts will be made without specific supporting studies.
dataRefs: Metodología de utilización de datos El proyecto seguirá tres niveles: Nivel 1: datos sintéticos. Se utilizarán para construir la interfaz, probar el procesamiento y demostrar escenarios de alerta. Nivel 2: datos científicos públicos. Se seleccionarán conjuntos de datos pertinentes de NASA OSDR y otras fuentes abiertas, verificando metadatos, licencias, población estudiada y limitaciones. Nivel 3: datos humanos autorizados. Solo se considerarían datos humanos identificables o de acceso controlado con las autorizaciones correspondientes. No se presupone acceso a historiales médicos privados de astronautas. Los datos de animales, cultivos celulares, microorganismos o modelos experimentales no se interpretarán automáticamente como equivalentes a datos clínicos humanos.
